_meta.indication: OCREVUS is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsing or primary progressive forms of multiple sclerosis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active controlled Phase III study with treatment duration of 96 weeks, comparing ocrelizumab 600 mg every 24 weeks to interferon beta-1a 44 µg SC.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Protocol-defined annualized relapse rate (ARR) by 96 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized relapse rate 0.156 (OCREVUS) vs 0.292 (REBIF); 46% relative reduction (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel-group, active controlled Phase III study of 96 weeks, ocrelizumab 600 mg every 24 weeks vs interferon beta-1a 44 µg SC (identical design to WA21092).
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Protocol-defined annualized relapse rate (ARR) by 96 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized relapse rate 0.155 (OCREVUS) vs 0.290 (REBIF); 47% relative reduction (p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study of ocrelizumab 600 mg (two 300 mg IV infusions 14 days apart) every 24 weeks vs placebo in adults with PPMS.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to onset of 12-week confirmed disability progression (CDP)
pivotal_trials.result: 12-week confirmed disability progression 32.9% (OCREVUS) vs 39.3% (placebo); 24% risk reduction, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.59, 0.98); p=0.0321.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were upper respiratory tract infections (RMS 40% vs 33% REBIF; PPMS 49% vs 43% placebo) and infusion reactions (RMS 34% vs 10%; PPMS 40% vs 26%). Warnings: infusion reactions, infections, and malignancies.
target_moa: Ocrelizumab is a recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody directed against CD20-expressing B-cells; following cell surface binding it results in antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-mediated lysis.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable and the clinical trial design is similar to that of trials of previously approved drugs for relapsing forms of MS.

requirement.text: 3194-6: Perform a shipping study to confirm validation of the commercial ocrelizumab drug product shipping conditions.

citations.quote: 3194-6 Perform a shipping study to confirm validation of the commercial ocrelizumab drug product shipping conditions. The study will be performed using representative shipping routes and drug product that has been stored for an extended period. The study will include testing of pre- and post-shipping samples for product quality (purity by SE-HPLC, reduced and non-reduced CE-SDS, IE-HPLC, sub-visible particles, visible particles, clarity/opalescence, and potency) and confirmation that the commercial shipping configuration minimizes physical damage to drug product containers.

requirement.text: 3194-12: Perform a leachable study to evaluate the drug product container closure system through end of shelf-life under recommended storage conditions.

citations.quote: 3194-12 Perform a leachable study to evaluate the drug product container closure system through the end of shelf-life when stored under the recommended conditions. Testing will be performed at regular intervals and will include appropriate methods to detect, identify, and quantify organic non-volatile (e.g., HPLC-UV-MS), volatile (e.g., headspace GC-MS) and semi-volatile (e.g., GC-MS) species and metals (e.g., ICP-MS). Study results will be updated annually in the BLA Annual Report. The complete data and risk evaluation for potential impact of leachables on product safety and quality will be submitted to the BLA.
